component GenTest3
import CompilerAlgebra.{ ... }
export Executable
trait Generator[\Exx\] excludes { Number, Character }
    map[\Gxx\](f: Exx->Gxx): Generator[\Gxx\]
end Generator


trait Condition[\E\] extends { Generator[\E\] }
    cond[\G\](t: E -> G, e: () -> G): G
    map[\G\](f: E->G): Condition[\G\] =
        cond(fn (e:E) => Just[\G\](f(e)), fn () => NothingObject[\G\])
end Condition


(* Maybe type *)

value trait Maybe[\E\] extends { Condition[\E\] }
        comprises { NothingObject[\E\], Just[\E\] }
end

value object Just[\E\](x: E) extends Maybe[\E\]
    getter asString(): String = "Just(" "XXX" ")"
    cond[\G\](t: E -> G, e: () -> G): G = t(x)
end

value object NothingObject[\E\] extends Maybe[\E\]
    getter asString():String = "Nothing"
    cond[\G\](t: E -> G, e: () -> G): G = e()
end


run(): () = println "PASS"

end

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

component_of () {
    # component/api name as declared, which is what `fortress run` wants
    sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*\(component\|api\)[[:space:]]\+\([A-Za-z0-9_.]\+\).*/\2/p' "$1" | head -1
}

run_one () {
    local corpus="$1" path="$2"
    local base name comp crc rrc t0 t1 ct rt
    base=$(basename "$path")
    name="${base%.*}"
    comp=$(component_of "$path")
    [ -n "$comp" ] || comp="$name"

    t0=$(date +%s)
    timeout -k 5 "$COMPILE_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress compile "$path" \
        > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.compile" 2>&1
    crc=$?
    t1=$(date +%s); ct=$((t1-t0))

    rrc=""
    rt=""
    if [ "$crc" -eq 0 ] && [ "${base##*.}" = "fss" ]; then
        t0=$(date +%s)
        timeout -k 5 "$RUN_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress run "$comp" \
            > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.run" 2>&1
        rrc=$?
        t1=$(date +%s); rt=$((t1-t0))
    fi

    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$corpus" "$base" "$comp" "$crc" "$rrc" "$ct" "$rt" >> "$TSV"
    echo "$corpus/$base crc=$crc rrc=$rrc ${ct}s"
}

main () {
    echo "=== ladder start $(date -Is) ==="
    disk_guard
    if [ ! -d "$PRISTINE" ]; then
        build_library
        rm -rf "$PRISTINE"; cp -a "$LADDER_CACHES" "$PRISTINE"
    fi
    sanity || { echo "SANITY FAILED: library_tests/Integer1 did not print PASS"; exit 1; }
    echo "sanity ok: library_tests/Integer1 compiles and prints PASS"
    prune_cache

    : > "$TSV"
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1

    local n=0 line corpus f
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r corpus f; do
        [ -n "$corpus" ] || continue
        run_one "$corpus" "$corpus/$f"
        n=$((n+1))
        rm -rf "${LADDER_TMP:?}"/fortress*rats
        if [ $((n % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then prune_cache; disk_guard; fi
    done < "$OUT/subset.txt"
    prune_cache
    echo "=== ladder done $(date -Is), $n files ==="
    disk_guard
}

main "$@"

component MaybeRungM
export Executable

(*) Both cases are chosen at run time, so a body that returned a constant or
(*) returned its own argument would not pass.
pick(b: Boolean): Maybe[\ZZ32\] = if b then Just[\ZZ32\](7) else NothingObject[\ZZ32\] end

run():() = do
    full = pick(true)
    empty = pick(false)

    (*) The empty case written as the unparameterised singleton and coerced
    (*) into Maybe, which is how Specification/basic/exceptions.tex:122 spells
    (*) the default of a Maybe field.
    coerced: Maybe[\ZZ32\] = Nothing

    assert(full.holds, "Just(7).holds")
    deny(empty.holds, "NothingObject[ZZ32].holds")
    deny(coerced.holds, "coerced Nothing.holds")

    deny(full.isNothing, "Just(7).isNothing")
    assert(empty.isNothing, "NothingObject[ZZ32].isNothing")
    assert(coerced.isNothing, "coerced Nothing.isNothing")

    assert(full.size, 1, "Just(7).size")
    assert(empty.size, 0, "NothingObject[ZZ32].size")

    assert(full.get, 7, "Just(7).get")
    assert(full.getDefault(3), 7, "Just(7).getDefault(3)")
    assert(empty.getDefault(3), 3, "NothingObject[ZZ32].getDefault(3)")
    assert(coerced.getDefault(3), 3, "coerced Nothing.getDefault(3)")

    (*) get on the empty case throws NotFound, as Condition declares.
    caught: Boolean := false
    try
        ignore(empty.get)
    catch e
        NotFound => caught := true
    end
    assert(caught, "NothingObject[ZZ32].get did not throw NotFound")

    (*) Dispatch through the trait's own method.
    assert(full.cond[\ZZ32\](fn (x:ZZ32):ZZ32 => x, fn ():ZZ32 => 0), 7, "cond on Just(7)")
    assert(empty.cond[\ZZ32\](fn (x:ZZ32):ZZ32 => x, fn ():ZZ32 => 0), 0, "cond on NothingObject")
    assert(coerced.cond[\ZZ32\](fn (x:ZZ32):ZZ32 => x, fn ():ZZ32 => 0), 0, "cond on coerced Nothing")

    (*) Dispatch on the run-time type.
    assert(typecase full of Just[\ZZ32\] => "just"; else => "other" end,
           "just", "typecase on Just(7)")
    assert(typecase empty of Just[\ZZ32\] => "just"; else => "other" end,
           "other", "typecase on NothingObject")

    (*) A Maybe is a generator: the empty case yields nothing, the full case
    (*) yields its one element.
    for x <- empty do fail("NothingObject[ZZ32] generated an element") end
    for x <- full do assert(x, 7, "for over Just(7)") end
    for x <- coerced do fail("coerced Nothing generated an element") end

    assert(full.reduce(fn (a:ZZ32, b:ZZ32):ZZ32 => a + b, 0), 7, "reduce over Just(7)")
    assert(empty.reduce(fn (a:ZZ32, b:ZZ32):ZZ32 => a + b, 0), 0, "reduce over NothingObject")

    assert(full.asString, "Just(7)", "Just(7).asString")
    assert(empty.asString, "Nothing", "NothingObject[ZZ32].asString")
    assert(coerced.asString, "Nothing", "coerced Nothing.asString")

    println "PASS"
end

end
EOF

cd /home/user/fortress-maybe && cat > explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/REPORT.md <<'MDEOF'
# Rung M: `Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing` for the compiler world

problem: `explorations/compile-ladder/after/raw/tests/oddJuxt.fss.compile:2` — "Function Nothing is not defined."; 472 further occurrences of "Maybe is undefined." across the ladder's recorded first errors, and the compiler prelude declares none of the three names.
spec: `Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:33-55` — the Convenience Types section declares `trait Maybe[\T\] comprises { Nothing, Just[\T\] }` with `isNothing: Boolean`, `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}`, and `object Just[\T\](just: T) extends Maybe[\T\]`; used at `Specification/basic/exceptions.tex:112-130`, which writes the defaults of two `Maybe` fields as `= Nothing`.
precedent: `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661` with bodies at `.fss:1308-1367` — the shipped `value trait Option[\E19\] extends { Condition[\E19\] } comprises { NoneObject[\E19\], Some[\E19\] }` with `coerce(_: None)` and `value object None end`, which is this protocol under other names and is the shape copied member for member; the team's own commented draft for these names is `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229`.
deviation: eight, each listed in §6 below; the first is that the specification's single non-parametric `Nothing` is realised as `NothingObject[\T\]` plus `value object Nothing end` plus `coerce(_: Nothing)`, because a `where` clause on an object declaration is refused by `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4088` (`forObjectDeclPrePass`, `header.getWhereClause().isNone()`), while coercion is the one mechanism this path has and the interpreter lacks.

## 1. What was inherited

Nothing. `git log --oneline cb242a2d8..HEAD` was empty and `git status --short` clean when this rung started, so there was no earlier attempt to verify; `tmp/` held no logs. Every check below was run in this worktree.

## 2. Where does this fix belong

`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:332` is the `Maybe` row: interpreter at `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:813-880`, compiler world "present at `CompilerLibrary.fsi:194-204` but wholly commented out; `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:648-660` ships `Option`/`Some`/`NoneObject` instead". The row's spec column names `library/default-libraries.tex`, which is an api rendering and therefore not evidence (`Specification/library/structure.tex:25-31`); the governing prose is `basic-lib/convenience.tex`, found by grepping the prose chapters (§3).

The declarations belong in the library, not in the compiler. `grep -rn` over `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler` and `runtimeSystem` for `Option`, `Some`, `None` and `NoneObject` finds nothing, so the protocol this copies is special-cased nowhere in Java or Scala; and `WellKnownNames.java:114-115` makes `CompilerLibrary` and `CompilerBuiltin` the compile path's implicit prelude, so a declaration in either is in scope for every compiled program. This rung therefore touches no `.java` and no `.scala`, and needs no `ant compileAll`.

Within the library, the choice was `Library/CompilerLibrary` (where the team's draft sits) over `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin` (where `Option` sits). The draft's location was followed. It works: `CompilerLibrary` already declares objects that extend a trait declared in `CompilerBuiltin` (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:66-103`, thirteen objects extending `UncheckedException`, which is `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:711`), which is exactly what `Maybe extends Condition[\T\]` needs, and the coercion works from there (§5). It also costs less to rebuild: editing `CompilerLibrary` rebuilds three components (41 s + 2 s + 2 s measured), editing `CompilerBuiltin` would rebuild five (145 s measured cold).

## For `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md`

Under **Execution model**, after the line on the code generator lowering every type to a
JVM reference type:

*Folded 2026-09-19 under "The compile-path ladder baseline" instead, after R1's lines,
because the gather brief places a rung's FACTS lines there and the two repair rungs belong
with the eight they repair; noted here so the placement is traceable.*

- **A numeral's value reaches the compiled world intact as of the repair batch of 2026-09-18.** `CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr` chose the numeral's representation by `BigInteger.bitLength()` against `<= 32` and `<= 64`; `bitLength()` counts no sign bit, so a non-negative numeral of bit length exactly 32 or exactly 64 was truncated into a signed slot and arrived wrapped negative — `4294967295` and `18446744073709551615` both became `-1`, against `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86` (a numeral of digits has the value of its digits in radix ten, with nothing bounding it) and `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370,398-401` (wrapping and saturating have their own operator spellings and "operations on type $\mathbb{Z}$ never need to wrap or saturate"). The bounds are now `<= 31` and `<= 63`, exact for both signs, and `FIntLiteral.asNN64` reads the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 now keeps. Where the compiled run contradicted `walk` in silence it now agrees with it: `4294967295` at `ZZ` prints `4294967295` on both paths, and `a = 4294967295; b = 1; println (a + b)` prints `4294967296` on both (ledger row 317, `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`).
- **A radix numeral is a natural number, not a bit pattern, and the compile path was the only place that pretended otherwise.** `literals.tex:104-108` gives a radix numeral the type `NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadix[[n,r,v]]` over the value of its digits in radix $r$, so `8000'0000_16` is $2^{31}$ and `A0000000_16` is $2684354560$; the interpreter has always refused such a numeral at a signed type ("RHS expression type Long is not assignable to LHS type ZZ32"), and the compile path accepted it only because the wrap turned it into something else. Five sites in the tree relied on that: `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:569,571` (`ZZ32_MIN`, `ZZ64_MIN`), `library_tests/Integer3.fss:46` and `Integer4.fss:46` (`twiceHuge`), and `library_tests/IntegerChoose2.fss:114` with its ungated twin `ChooseTest3.fss:125`. The first four are repaired value-for-value; the fifth was not only illegal but was exercising `i = -1257966796` instead of the $\sqrt{2^{63}}$ boundary its own comment names.
- Every numeral in the corpora and the libraries whose value has bit length exactly 32 or exactly 64 is enumerated, by value and in every radix, at `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/boundary-numerals.txt`; eighteen of the enumerated lines are on the compile path, twelve of them in range for their annotated type and right until now only by the wrap's accident. A decimal-only grep misses the radix-16 half, which is where four of the five out-of-range sites were, and where the `Integer.test` failures came from.
- **The repair turns one loud failure into a quiet value, and the value it prints is wrong even though the value it holds is right.** `FIntLiteral.asNN64` threw for every string-carried numeral before this rung, and `simpleIntLiteralArith.fromBigInteger` sends every `IntLiteral` arithmetic result of bit length 64 or more to the string branch (`nativeHelpers/simpleIntLiteralArith.java:31-32`), a path R2 does not touch — so the transition needs no numeral of bit length 64 in the source at all. `x = 9223372036854775807` then `n: NN64 = x + x + 1` raised `Error: Not in range for NN64: 18446744073709551615` before R2 and now computes $2^{64}-1$, which `literals.tex:83-86` makes the correct value, and prints it as `-1` because `FNN64.toString` is signed (`compiler/runtimeValues/FNN64.java:20`, ledger row 326). The probe is `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/skeptic/s3.fss` with `s3.compiled` and `s3.walk`; `walk` refuses the coercion instead ("RHS expression type Long is not assignable to LHS type NN64"). The error that named the true value is gone while the rendering is wrong, so row 326 and this fact are one situation and should be read together.
- The bytecode optimizer's `RemoveLiteralCoercions` substitution (`FIntLiteral.make(I)` plus `coerce_ZZ32` becomes `FZZ32.make(I)`, `RemoveLiteralCoercions.java:33-53`) elides `asZZ32`'s range check, which is sound exactly when the code generator's int branch is the `ZZ32`-representable range: false under `l <= 32`, true under `l <= 31`. The optimizer is dormant — reached only from `ByteCodeOptimizer.main` (`ByteCodeOptimizer.java:130,146`), nothing in `Shell` or the compiler driver calls it, its 226 tests off at `default_repository/configuration:50-51` (`map/dormant-code.md:188`) — so this is a latent soundness fact, not live behaviour.

## For `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`

### Row 317 — amend in place

Row 317 is not renumbered and not moved; its existing text stands, with one correction and
one closing paragraph appended to its last column.

**The correction.** In the sentence beginning "Through a **declared** binding it predates
rung 6 and is reached by the coercion `ZZ64.coerce(x: IntLiteral) = x.asZZ64`", the citation
`CompilerBuiltin.fss:557` is stale: that line is now the comment above `ceilingAverage`, and
the `ZZ64` coercion is at `CompilerBuiltin.fss:562`.

**Append to the row's last column:**

> Four things this row did not say. The `ZZ` half: `ZZ.coerce(x: IntLiteral) = x.asZZ` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:501`) renders the wrapped value, so `a: ZZ = 4294967295` was `-1` in the type the specification defines as all the finite integers (`compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/r2a.compiled.before`). The defeated `ZZ32` diagnostic: `asZZ32`'s range check is applied to the already-wrapped value and passes on `-1`, so `a: ZZ32 = 4294967295` silently became `-1` instead of raising "Not in range for ZZ32" (`probes/r2c.compiled.before`). The second specification citation: `basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370` and `:398-401` give wrapping and saturating their own operator spellings and say ordinary operations "never need to wrap or saturate". And the coupling: `FIntLiteral.asNN32` (`:79-83`) and `asNN64` (`:85-95`) read the wrapped two's-complement pattern as the right unsigned value, so a repair to the code generator alone makes `asNN64` throw (measured: `probes/junit-codegen-only.out`). **Repaired 2026-09-18** by the repair batch's R2 (`compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`): the two bounds become `<= 31` and `<= 63`, exact for both signs and the form rung 7's own `simpleIntLiteralArith.java:30-33` already used; `asNN64` learns to read `largerVal`; and `asNN32`'s range check, which masked its argument to 32 bits and so accepted everything including the `BOGUS` sentinel, is made to mean what it says. `p37a`, `p39`, `r2a` and `r2e` now give the same answer compiled as under `walk`, and three diagnostics the wrap had defeated are restored (`probes/r2c`, `r2d`, `r2f`). `p37` does **not** agree and the first version of this amendment wrongly said it did: compiled it now raises `Not in range for ZZ64: 18446744073709551615` where `walk` prints three `false` lines, because `trait IntLiteral`'s comparisons are performed at `ZZ64` (row 328 below); before the repair it answered `true`, silently wrong. The repair uncovered five sites that relied on the wrap and closed four of them; the fifth is row 327 below. What it does **not** settle is which number type an untyped numeral's arithmetic happens at: the branch chooses an overload of `FIntLiteral.make`, never a type, and every numeral still has the one flat static type `Types.INT_LITERAL` (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:467-468`), so that fork is untouched and still open.

### Four new rows, numbered 325-328

R1 of this batch was folded first and took 319-324, so the three rows this rung proposed as
319, 320 and 321 are **325, 326 and 327**, and the fourth row, required by the skeptic's
correction 2, is **328**. `SKEPTIC.md` refers to the first three by their proposed numbers.

**325.** *A numeral outside a bounded integer type is a run-time error on the compile path where the specification makes it a static one.* NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, implementation gap. `literals.tex:83-86` gives a digits-only numeral the type `NaturalNumeral[[n,10,v]]` carrying its value $v$, and `:104-108` the same for a radix numeral, so `a: ZZ32 = 4294967295` is a static error; the checker instead gives every numeral the one flat type `Types.INT_LITERAL` (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:467-468`) and the compiler world's `trait IntLiteral` has six abstract getters and no static parameter (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:370-376`), so nothing in the static types carries the value a checker could range-check. Probes `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/r2c.fss`, `r2d.fss`, `r2f.fss`, `r2g.fss`, `r2h.fss`, both ways: each compiles clean and raises `Not in range for ZZ32/NN32/ZZ64` at run time, and each is refused by the interpreter at the point of use. Ours. The fix is a static parameter on `IntLiteral` in the compiler prelude and a range check in the checker's literal case; it is a checker-and-prelude rung and was outside R2's scope. Before R2 these five programs did not raise at all — they truncated in silence — so this row is the improved half of what row 317 repaired, not a regression.

**326.** *`NN32` and `NN64` render their values signed on the compile path.* NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, implementation gap. `FNN32.toString` is `String.valueOf(val)` over a signed `int` (`compiler/runtimeValues/FNN32.java:19-20`) and `FNN64.toString` is `"" + val` over a signed `long` (`FNN64.java:20`), so an unsigned value above the type's signed half prints negative: `n32: NN32 = 4294967295` and `n64: NN64 = 18446744073709551615` both print `-1` (`compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/r2b.compiled.before` and `.after`, unchanged by R2). The values themselves are right — `compiler_tests/IntLiteralWrapRepairR2.fss:64,69` assert `n32 = h32u + h32u + one32u` and `n64 = h64u + h64u + one64u` and both pass — so this is rendering only. Ours. The fix is `Integer.toUnsignedString` and `Long.toUnsignedString` in those two classes, plus whatever `NN32.asString` and `NN64.asString` reach in the prelude; the interpreter has no comparable site because it refuses the coercion from a numeral to `NN32`/`NN64` altogether (`probes/r2b.walk.before`). Independent of row 317 and untouched by its repair.

**327.** *`library_tests/ChooseTest3.fss:125` exercises a negative binomial coefficient where it means the algorithm's fast/slow boundary.* NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, defect in a test. `verifyChoose(3037000500+j, 2)` inside `for j <- seq(-3:3)` coerces the numeral at `ZZ32`, because `j` is a `ZZ32` and `3037000500` is outside `ZZ32`; the comment two lines above at `:122-123` says these are "the points that separate use of the fast `ZZ64` algorithm from the slow, cautious algorithm". Under the code generator's wrap the call was `verifyChoose(-1257966796+j, 2)`, so the boundary the file names was never tested, and both sides of `verifyChoose`'s assertions used the same wrong value, which is why nothing showed. The fix is the one R2 applied to the identical line in `IntegerChoose2.fss:114`: bind the constant at `ZZ64` first, which is the file's own idiom. `ChooseTest3.fss` is named in no `.test` file and `LibraryJUTest.java:36` sweeps `.test` files only, so no gate covers it and no measurement of a repair to it is available; R2 left it rather than edit it unverified. Ours.

**328.** *`IntLiteral` comparison is performed at `ZZ64`, so comparing a numeral outside `ZZ64` throws where the specification requires an answer.* NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, implementation gap. `trait IntLiteral`'s six comparison operators are each `self.asZZ64 <op> other.asZZ64` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:837-842`, rung 6's repair), and `FIntLiteral.asZZ64` raises for a numeral carried as a decimal string (`compiler/runtimeValues/FIntLiteral.java:74-77`, the message built at `:63-65`), so `a = 18446744073709551615; a < 5` dies with `Not in range for ZZ64: 18446744073709551615` where `literals.tex:83-86` gives the numeral its exact value and requires `false`, which is what `walk` prints. Probe `explorations/compiler-probes/p37.fss` both ways, outputs at `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/probes/skeptic/p37.walk.skeptic` (three `false` lines) and `p37.compiled.skeptic` (the error, from `asZZ64`); `p37a`, whose numerals are inside `ZZ64`, agrees on both paths. Found by R2's skeptic. Until R2 the code generator's wrap hid this: a numeral of bit length 64 became `-1`, the comparison answered `true`, and the program was silently wrong — so R2 replaced a quiet wrong answer with a loud one, which is the better of the two and is why the row is opened rather than the repair narrowed. The fix is comparison over the value in `BigInteger`, the shape `simpleIntLiteralArith.java:26-27` already uses (`new BigInteger(a.toString())`); outside R2's scope.
